newsitem.title: GREECE: UK ISSUES TRAVEL ADVISORY ON CORFU AFTER KILLING.
newsitem.headline: UK ISSUES TRAVEL ADVISORY ON CORFU AFTER KILLING.

text.p: Britain warned its citizens on Friday about dangerous boat thieves on Greece's holiday island of Corfu after a tourist was shot dead, allegedly by a raiding party from neighbouring Albania.
The travel advisory warns British tourists visiting Corfu by boat to stay in harbours where their craft can be guarded and says that visitors should avoid marinas from midnight to 6 a.m.
"On 26 September a British resident of Corfu was shot and killed ... by criminals attempting to steal a boat," said the advisory.

"This incident, following on from an earlier incident in June when shots were fired at a tourist hotel, comfirms the continuing threat posed by boat thieves," the advisory, obtained from the British embassy, said.
British tourist Keith Hedley, 57, from Kent was shot dead by the thieves when he tried to stop them from stealing a power dinghy tied to his yacht in the early hours of the morning.
The Foreign Office issued a warning to British holidaymakers three months ago after boat thieves opened fire with automatic weapons on a coastal holiday resort on Corfu.
Police said gangs of boat thieves operate from the nearby Albanian coast and they suspected the gunmen who killed Hedley to have crossed from Albania.
They said the gunmen, aboard a speedboat, headed straight for Albania, eight kms (4.8 miles) away, after the incident.
Hedley was docked at Gouvia marina, near the main town of Corfu. He was asleep with three friends on the yacht when he heard the thieves and interrupted them, police said.
